Shanghai/Ningbo.note: The primary event name moves from Saudel to Krovanh this run, and the reason is mechanical rather than editorial: Saudel has crossed to the South China Sea and is no longer the system near the Yangtze delta, while Krovanh is, with a 510 km closest approach at +45h. The backlog itself is unchanged and still Saudel's. Linerlytica's 30 Aug snapshot has Shanghai/Ningbo at 1.68m TEU on 288.5 ships at anchorage with a queue-to-berth ratio of 3.24, up from 2.53 the previous day — the queue was still building on the last day the source published, so nothing here justifies dropping the entry. Xiamen.note: Saudel's closest approach to any tracked port this run — 99 km, right now. SEKO has Xiamen gates open with Taiwan Strait swell rolling scheduled feeder sailings, and no source reports a terminal suspension or a berth waiting figure, so the status stays watch and both wait fields stay null. Saudel is forecast to weaken to a tropical depression within 24 hours as it moves away to the west-southwest, so this entry should be a candidate for eventEnded on the next run if the system leaves the JMA feed.

remarks: Two active tropical storms, neither of them closing any port. Saudel sits 99 km off Xiamen and is forecast to weaken to a depression within 24 hours as it drifts toward eastern Guangdong; Krovanh is east of Okinawa and never gets closer than 510 km to Shanghai/Ningbo.

The congestion at Shanghai and Ningbo is now a backlog story rather than a weather story. Both ports have been open since 28 August, and the 7-10+ day berth queues are the accumulated bunching from Saudel's landfall rather than any current closure.

No source published a fresh waiting-time figure in the 24 hours before this run — SEKO is still on its 1 September revision and Kuehne+Nagel has no port update for 1 or 2 September. Every wait figure here is carried at its 1 September vintage and none has been re-estimated.
Linerlytica has not published a congestion snapshot since 30 August, so the queue figures behind the site's rankings are four days old.
